senses.title: At the end of something
senses.definition: placed or happening at the end of a line, journey, or structure
senses.definitionCN: 位于线、旅程或结构的末端
senses.example: The train stopped at the terminal station.
senses.exampleCN: 列车停在终点站。
senses.why: The root means boundary: whatever is terminal touches the final mark.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「界标」：凡 terminal 之物都触到了最后的界线。

senses.title: Of an illness that ends in death
senses.definition: describing an illness that cannot be cured and will cause death
senses.definitionCN: 形容无法治愈、将致死亡的疾病
senses.example: The doctor told him the illness was terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 医生告诉他病已到晚期。
senses.why: Life itself reaches its boundary; the end mark falls on the body.
senses.whyCN: 生命本身抵达界线：终点标记落在了身体上。

senses.title: A point where a line ends or meets
senses.definition: a point where wires or systems connect or end
senses.definitionCN: 线路连接或终止之点
senses.example: Check the battery terminals before starting.
senses.exampleCN: 启动前检查电池接线端。
senses.why: A boundary is also a contact point: where a line stops, another may begin.
senses.whyCN: 界线也是接触点：一条线停驻之处，另一条线可以开始。

senses.title: A building for passengers or goods at the end of a route
senses.definition: a building at an airport, port, or bus station where journeys end or start
senses.definitionCN: 机场、港口或车站里旅程开始或结束的建筑
senses.example: The airport terminal opened at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 航站楼在黎明开放。
senses.why: The endpoint of a route grows walls and roofs; the boundary becomes a place.
senses.whyCN: 路线的端点长出墙与屋顶：界线变成了场所。

senses.title: A device for entering a computer system
senses.definition: a screen and keyboard connected to a main computer or network
senses.definitionCN: 连接主机或网络的屏幕与键盘设备
senses.example: She logged in at a library terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 她在图书馆的终端机上登录。
senses.why: The device sits at the edge of the network, where the user touches the system.
senses.whyCN: 设备位于网络边缘，正是用户触碰系统之处，故称终端。

senses.title: Final and not open to change
senses.definition: final, forming the end of a series or process
senses.definitionCN: 构成系列或过程之终点的
senses.example: The court made a terminal ruling in the case.
senses.exampleCN: 法院就本案作出终局裁定。
senses.why: Once the boundary is crossed, nothing continues beyond it.
senses.whyCN: 界线一旦越过，其后便再无延续。

intro.en: Terminal comes from Latin terminalis, of a boundary, built on terminus, the boundary stone or end point.
intro.cn: terminal 源自拉丁语 terminalis「属于界标的」，词基 terminus 意为界石、端点。

items.en: Terminus was the god and the stone of boundaries in Roman fields.
items.cn: terminus 是罗马田界之神，也指界石。

items.en: Terminalis meant belonging to a boundary or end.
items.cn: terminalis 意为属于边界或端点的。

items.en: The deeper origin of terminus before Latin is uncertain; a link with words for stake or mark has been suggested.
items.cn: terminus 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定；有说法将其联系到「木桩、标记」。

items.en: English borrowed terminal in the fifteenth century for words ending a clause or a limb tip.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪借入 terminal，先指从句末词与肢体末端。

items.en: Railways gave the station sense, medicine the fatal sense, computing the device sense.
items.cn: 铁路带来终点站义，医学带来晚期义，计算带来终端机义。

note.en: Terminal is compared with its Latin family and with words of ending.
note.cn: 把 terminal 与拉丁词族及表示终结的词对比。

normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：界石 terminus、机场大厅、电池接点、晚期疾病。

normal.en: Terminus was a stone at the edge of the field: terminal is anything at the edge.

normal.en: Terminal Two: the end of the air route has a building.
normal.cn: 二号航站楼：航线终点长出了建筑。

normal.en: Battery terminals are where the current ends and begins.

normal.en: A computer terminal is the edge of the network.
normal.cn: 计算机终端是网络的边缘。

normal.en: Terminal illness: the life line reaches its last mark.
normal.cn: 晚期疾病：生命之线到达最后刻度。

abstract.en: Every line owns one point where it stops pretending.
abstract.cn: 每条线都拥有一个不再假装延伸的点。

abstract.en: A boundary is a door: it can end a journey or begin one.
abstract.cn: 边界是一扇门：可以终结旅程，也可以开启旅程。

abstract.en: Endings do not always mean death; sometimes they mean arrival.
abstract.cn: 终点未必意味着死亡；有时意味着抵达。

examples.en: The ferry terminal was crowded with summer travellers.
examples.cn: 渡轮码头挤满了夏季旅客。

examples.en: New treatment gave hope even to patients with terminal illness.
examples.cn: 新疗法甚至给晚期患者带来希望。

examples.en: Loose terminals made the radio fail.
examples.cn: 接线端松动导致收音机失灵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone marking where the road stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：标记道路止步之处的一块石头。

branches.en: Routes end in buildings that hold the boundary.
branches.cn: 路线终结于承载边界的建筑。

branches.en: The body reaches its own boundary stone.
branches.cn: 身体抵达自己的界石。

branches.en: Where a line ends, contact begins.
branches.cn: 线止之处，接触开始。

branches.en: The user sits at the network's edge.
branches.cn: 用户坐在网络边缘。

branches.en: A ruling that closes the file for good.
branches.cn: 一笔永久归档的终局裁定。

definition_zh: 白蚁；（喻）从内部慢慢蛀空组织的人或事物
definition_en: a pale, soft-bodied social insect that feeds on wood and lives in colonies with distinct castes
core_image: 一块外表完好的木板被撬开，里面是无数细小管道，像被谁用针一层层掏空，只剩一层薄壳
scene: 老房子的地板踩上去还是硬的，可撬开一角，底下已经全是细土一样的碎渣。 One termite is harmless, but a colony can hollow a beam without touching its surface.
sceneCN: 这里 termite 指「白蚁」（第 1 个义项：体色浅、体软、蛀食木材的群居昆虫）；句意为一只白蚁无害，但一个蚁群能在不碰表面的情况下把梁掏空。

pos.zh: 白蚁；白蚁类

senses.title: The pale wood-eating social insect
senses.titleCN: 浅色、蛀食木材的群居昆虫
senses.definition: a soft-bodied, usually pale insect of the cockroach lineage that lives in colonies and feeds mainly on wood
senses.definitionCN: 体软、通常色浅、属蟑螂谱系、群居并以木材为主食的昆虫
senses.example: One termite is harmless, but a colony can hollow a beam.
senses.exampleCN: 一只白蚁无害，但一个蚁群能把梁掏空。
senses.why: the word names the animal, and the whole vocabulary of damage, mounds and castes is built outward from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名动物，关于损坏、蚁丘与品级的整套词汇都由它向外生长出来。

senses.title: The colony with its castes
senses.definition: the organised society of workers, soldiers and reproductives living in one nest
senses.definitionCN: 在同一巢中生活的工蚁、兵蚁与繁殖个体组成的有组织社会
senses.example: The termite colony was three metres deep and twenty years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这个白蚁群深达三米，已有二十年。
senses.why: because individuals are almost never seen alone, the singular often stands for the whole society.
senses.whyCN: 因为个体几乎从不单独出现，单数常代指整个社会。

senses.title: A named ecological type
senses.definition: a kind identified by habit, such as subterranean, drywood or mound-building termites
senses.definitionCN: 按习性区分的类型，如地下白蚁、干木白蚁、筑丘白蚁
senses.example: Drywood termites need no contact with soil at all.
senses.exampleCN: 干木白蚁完全不需要接触土壤。
senses.why: types are distinguished by where they live, so a qualifier carries the whole difference.
senses.whyCN: 类型由栖息处区分，因此一个限定语承担了全部差别。

senses.title: A destroyer of timber in buildings
senses.definition: the species regarded as a structural pest because it consumes wood from the inside
senses.definitionCN: 因从内部吃空木材而被视为结构害虫的物种
senses.example: Termite damage went unnoticed until the floor sagged.
senses.exampleCN: 白蚁的损坏直到地板下沉才被发现。
senses.why: the damage is described by its agent because the insect leaves a hollow shell rather than a visible hole.
senses.whyCN: 损坏由施害者来描述，因为昆虫留下的是空壳而不是明显的洞。

senses.title: A decomposer of dead wood
senses.definition: the ecological role of breaking down fallen timber and returning nutrients to the soil
senses.definitionCN: 分解倒木、把养分归还土壤的生态角色
senses.example: Termites clear dead wood faster than fungi in dry forests.
senses.exampleCN: 在干燥森林里，白蚁分解枯木比真菌更快。
senses.why: the same activity that ruins a house recycles a forest, so the word carries both judgements.
senses.whyCN: 毁屋与还林是同一种活动，因此这个词同时承载两种判断。

senses.title: A subject for symbiosis research
senses.definition: the insect as a host whose gut microbes digest wood, studied as a model of symbiosis
senses.definitionCN: 肠道微生物帮它消化木材，因而作为共生模型被研究的昆虫
senses.example: The termite depends on microbes it passes to its young.
senses.exampleCN: 白蚁依赖它传给后代的微生物。
senses.why: a striking biological dependency makes the animal a research system, and the name stands for the system.
senses.whyCN: 一种显著的生物依赖使这种动物成为研究体系，其名称代表这个体系。

senses.title: A builder of ventilated mounds
senses.titleCN: 建造通风蚁丘的建筑者
senses.definition: the mound-building species whose structures regulate heat and gas exchange
senses.definitionCN: 所筑结构能调节热量与气体交换的筑丘物种
senses.example: The termite mound keeps a steady temperature through the day.
senses.exampleCN: 白蚁丘昼夜保持稳定温度。
senses.why: architecture is attributed to a builder, so the insect's name travels to the structure it makes.
senses.whyCN: 建筑被归给建造者，因此昆虫之名也移向它所造的结构。

senses.title: Figurative: something hollowing from within
senses.definition: figurative, a person or institution that undermines a group secretly and gradually
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指暗中、逐步蛀空某个群体的人或机构
senses.example: The report called the smuggling network a termite in the customs service.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把走私网络称作海关内部的白蚁。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the hidden, internal, gradual hollowing, which is exactly what the insect does.
senses.whyCN: 比喻只保留隐蔽、内部、渐进的掏空，而这正是这种昆虫所做的事。

intro.en: Termite is a late eighteenth-century learned word from Latin termes, the name for a woodworm; its earlier English name was the misleading white ant.
intro.cn: termite 是 18 世纪后期的学术词，出自拉丁 termes「木蠹虫」；其较早英语名是易致误解的 white ant。

items.en: Latin termes named a woodworm or a gnawing insect, and English naturalists revived it for the tropical wood-eating insect.
items.cn: 拉丁 termes 指木蠹虫或蛀咬的昆虫，英语博物学家把它复活用于热带蛀木昆虫。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the origin of Latin termes itself is unresolved; a link to a verb for gnawing has been suggested, but the form given for it is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：拉丁 termes 本身的来源无定论；与某个表示「啃咬」的动词的联系属提议，且所给形式为重构。

items.en: The older English name white ant treated the insect as a pale ant, a mistake that modern classification has corrected.
items.cn: 较早的英语名 white ant 把它当作浅色的蚂蚁，这一错误已被现代分类纠正。

items.en: Termites are now placed with cockroaches rather than with ants, a result of twentieth-century anatomical and molecular work.
items.cn: 白蚁现被归入蟑螂一类而非蚂蚁，这是 20 世纪解剖与分子研究的结果。

items.en: As timber construction spread, the word became a household word for structural damage and for the inspection trade.
items.cn: 随着木结构建筑普及，这个词成为关于结构损坏与检查行业的日常词。

items.en: The image of hidden internal hollowing produced the political metaphor of a termite inside an institution.
items.cn: 隐蔽内部掏空的意象产生了「机构内部白蚁」的政治比喻。

note.en: Group one separates termite from the insects it is historically confused with; group two separates the animal from its products and its metaphors.
note.cn: 第一组区分 termite 与其历史上易混的昆虫；第二组区分动物本身与其产物、比喻。

entries.definition: The insect once called a white ant; ants are darker, have a narrow waist and belong to a different order.
entries.definitionCN: 曾被叫作白蚁的昆虫；蚂蚁颜色更深、腰细，且属另一目。

entries.definition: An old English name for the termite, still met in older books; the insect is neither white nor an ant.
entries.definitionCN: 白蚁的旧英语名，仍见于旧书；它既不白也不是蚂蚁。

entries.definition: The nest or mound itself, not the insect; the -arium suffix marks a place.
entries.definitionCN: 巢或丘本身，而非昆虫；-arium 后缀标记场所。

entries.definition: A product that kills termites, built with the -cide suffix of killing.
entries.definitionCN: 杀白蚁的产品，由表「杀」的 -cide 后缀构成。

entries.definition: Woodworm names the larvae of wood-boring beetles; Latin termes covered similar gnawers before it was fixed to termites.
entries.definitionCN: woodworm 指蛀木甲虫的幼虫；拉丁 termes 在被固定指白蚁前也涵盖类似的蛀虫。

entries.definition: A carpenter ant excavates galleries in wood but does not eat it; a termite actually digests the wood.
entries.definitionCN: 木匠蚁在木中挖道但不吃木；白蚁则真正消化木材。

entries.definition: Borer names any animal that drills into wood or stems; termite names a particular social insect.
entries.definitionCN: borer 指任何钻入木材或茎的动物；termite 指特定的社会性昆虫。

entries.definition: Decomposer is a functional role in a food web; termite is the organism that fills it in dry forests.
entries.definitionCN: decomposer 是食物网中的功能角色；白蚁是在干燥森林中承担该角色的生物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin source, the real misnomer and real trade terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁来源、真实误称与真实行业用语。

normal.en: Latin termes meant a woodworm, and English took it for the tropical wood-eater.
normal.cn: 拉丁 termes 指木蠹虫，英语用它指热带的蛀木者。

normal.en: The old name white ant is a double mistake: not white, not an ant.
normal.cn: 旧名 white ant 是双重错误：既不白，也不是蚂蚁。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: termite damage, termite mound, termite inspection.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：白蚁损坏、白蚁丘、白蚁检查。

normal.en: Termites are now classified with cockroaches, not with ants.
normal.cn: 白蚁现被归入蟑螂一类，而非蚂蚁。

normal.en: Termites digest wood with microbes in their gut, a standard case of symbiosis.
normal.cn: 白蚁靠肠道微生物消化木材，是共生的标准案例。

abstract.en: Picture a beam that sounds solid when tapped and is dust inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一根梁，敲起来是实的，里面却是粉。

abstract.en: Picture a city of narrow corridors built without a single window.
abstract.cn: 想象一座全是窄走廊、没有一扇窗的城市。

abstract.en: Picture a flaw that eats an organisation while its reports look clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一个缺陷在吞噬机构，而报告看起来一切正常。

examples.en: Termites reached the sill through a mud tube built in the dark.
examples.cn: 白蚁沿着在暗处筑成的泥管到达了门槛。

examples.en: The mound was opened and the termites were gone within an hour.
examples.cn: 蚁丘被打开后，白蚁一小时内就撤空了。

examples.en: Inspectors look for termites before any sale of the house.
examples.cn: 房屋出售前，检查人员会找白蚁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ter（土）+ mite」——在土里做巢、把木头蛀成粉的虫 → 白蚁

root: 拉丁 termes「木蠹虫、蛀虫」，英语在 18 世纪后期借入指白蚁；拉丁词本身的更深来源不确定，与「啃咬」动词的联系仅为重构性提议。旧英语名 white ant 属误称。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hidden hollowing: a pale insect eats wood from inside, and the word then names the colony, a type, a structural pest, a decomposer, a symbiosis model, a mound builder, and finally a person who undermines from within.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种隐蔽的掏空展开：浅色昆虫从内部吃木；词语随后指群体、类型、结构害虫、分解者、共生模型、筑丘者，最后指从内部蛀空的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam that looks intact until the shell is lifted and only dust remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根看似完好的梁，撬开薄壳后只剩粉末。

branches.en: INSECT AND SOCIETY: one animal, then the caste system it never leaves.
branches.cn: 昆虫与社会：一只动物，然后是它从不脱离的品级体系。

branches.en: HABIT TYPES: subterranean, drywood and mound builders are one word plus a qualifier.
branches.cn: 习性命型：地下、干木、筑丘都是一个词加限定语。

branches.en: TWO VERDICTS: destroyer of a building, restorer of a forest.
branches.cn: 两种裁断：建筑的破坏者，森林的恢复者。

branches.en: RESEARCH AND ARCHITECTURE: the gut microbes and the ventilated mound.
branches.cn: 研究与建筑：肠道微生物与通风的蚁丘。

branches.en: HIDDEN CORROSION: the insect becomes an accusation about institutions.
branches.cn: 隐蔽腐蚀：昆虫变成对机构的指控。

intro.en: Termite is a learned Latin borrowing with no English prefix; its family is built with Latin and Greek suffixes.
intro.cn: termite 是拉丁学术借词，无英语前缀；其词族由拉丁与希腊后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin termes gives termite and termitarium; Greek isopteron 'equal wing' gives the old order name Isoptera.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 termes 提供 termite 与 termitarium；希腊 isopteron「等翅」提供旧目名 Isoptera。

items.example: The Latin word named a wood-eater long before the tropics were studied.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词早在热带被研究之前就指蛀木者。

items.example: The termite builds tubes of mud.
items.exampleCN: 白蚁筑泥管。

items.example: Termites worked through the floor.
items.exampleCN: 白蚁把地板吃穿了。

items.example: The termitarium rose two metres.
items.exampleCN: 白蚁巢高出两米。

items.example: The soil was treated with a termiticide.
items.exampleCN: 土壤用杀白蚁剂处理过。

items.example: The damage was termitic in origin.
items.exampleCN: 这项损坏源自白蚁。

items.example: Isoptera is the older order name for termites.
items.exampleCN: Isoptera 是白蚁的旧目名。

items.example: Isopterology has few specialists.
items.exampleCN: 研究白蚁的专家很少。

items.example: White ant appears only in older texts.
items.exampleCN: white ant 只见于较旧的文本。

definition_zh: 地形；地势；一片土地的自然特征
definition_en: the physical features and surface of a tract of land, especially as they affect movement or use
core_image: 越野车在碎石坡上颠簸前行，车轮下是坑洼与松石
scene: 越野车驶上碎石坡，车身随坑洼剧烈起伏，司机不断换挡： The jeep struggled over rough terrain full of loose stones.
sceneCN: 这里 terrain 指「一片土地的地形与地表状况」（第 1 个义项：土地的自然起伏与表面特征）；句意为越野车在遍布松石的崎岖地形中艰难前行。

pos.zh: 地形；地势；地带（可数或不可数，复数为 terrains）

senses.title: The physical features of land
senses.titleCN: 土地的自然起伏与表面特征
senses.definition: the shape, slope, and surface of a piece of land, including hills, rocks, and gullies
senses.definitionCN: 一片土地的形状、坡度与表面，包括山丘、岩石与冲沟
senses.example: The jeep struggled over rough terrain full of loose stones.
senses.exampleCN: 越野车在遍布松石的崎岖地形中艰难前行。
senses.why: Terrain comes from Latin terra 'earth', so it names the earth as something you must cross rather than something you own.
senses.whyCN: terrain 来自拉丁语 terra「土地」，因此它把土地命名为需要穿越的东西，而非拥有的东西。

senses.title: A tract of land for a purpose
senses.titleCN: 供某种用途的一片土地
senses.definition: an area of land considered as a unit for building, farming, or military use
senses.definitionCN: 作为建设、耕作或军事用途单位来考虑的一片土地
senses.example: The engineers surveyed the terrain before laying the foundation.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在打地基前勘测了这片土地。
senses.why: A tract becomes terrain when its physical character matters to what you plan to do on it.
senses.whyCN: 当一片土地的自然特征影响你打算做的事时，它就成为 terrain。

senses.title: Ground that affects movement
senses.definition: the surface conditions that help or hinder travel, especially for vehicles and troops
senses.definitionCN: 帮助或阻碍通行、尤其影响车辆与部队行动的地面状况
senses.example: The tanks slowed in the soft terrain near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 坦克在河边的松软地形中减速。
senses.why: Military usage made terrain a technical term: what the ground does to movement, not how it looks in a picture.
senses.whyCN: 军事用法使 terrain 成为技术术语：地面如何影响行动，而非照片上好不好看。

senses.title: Rough and difficult country
senses.definition: land that is broken, steep, or obstructed enough to make travel slow and dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 破碎、陡峭或受阻到使行进缓慢危险的土地
senses.example: Rescuers carried the injured climber across difficult terrain.
senses.exampleCN: 救援者抬着受伤的攀登者穿越难行地形。
senses.why: The word often carries an adjective of difficulty because terrain is defined by resistance to movement.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常与「困难」类形容词连用，因为 terrain 的定义就与对移动的阻力有关。

senses.title: Land represented in a model
senses.definition: a digital or physical representation of the land surface used in planning, games, or simulation
senses.definitionCN: 用于规划、游戏或仿真的地表数字或实体再现
senses.example: The game renders terrain down to individual boulders.
senses.exampleCN: 游戏把地形渲染到每一块巨石。
senses.why: Once land is data, terrain means the surface mesh: elevation, slope, and texture stored in a file.
senses.whyCN: 当土地变成数据，terrain 就指表面网格：存于文件中的高程、坡度与纹理。

senses.title: Habitat defined by ground features
senses.titleCN: 由地面特征定义的栖息地
senses.definition: the physical ground conditions that determine which species can live in an area
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪些物种能在某地生存的地面物理条件
senses.example: The lizard prefers rocky terrain with deep crevices.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蜥蜴偏好有深裂缝的岩石地形。
senses.why: For a small animal, slope and rock size are not scenery but shelter, so terrain becomes habitat.
senses.whyCN: 对小动物而言，坡度与石块大小不是风景，而是庇护所，因此地形成为栖息地。

senses.title: Abstract: an unfamiliar field
senses.definition: a field of knowledge or activity, pictured as ground to be crossed
senses.definitionCN: 被想象成需要穿越的地面的知识或活动领域
senses.example: The book leads readers through uncharted terrain in philosophy.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书带读者穿越哲学中未标注的领域。
senses.why: The metaphor treats knowledge as landscape: some parts are mapped, others are rough and unknown.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把知识当作地貌：有些部分已测绘，另一些则崎岖未知。

senses.title: Ski and outdoor park terrain
senses.definition: constructed or natural ground features used for skiing, biking, or off-road recreation
senses.definitionCN: 用于滑雪、骑行或越野休闲的人工或天然地面特征
senses.example: The resort opened a new terrain park for beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 度假村为初学者新开了一座地形公园。
senses.why: Recreation borrows the word for shaped ground: jumps, rails, and slopes are terrain made on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 休闲领域借这个词指被塑形的地面：跳台、栏杆与坡面都是刻意造出的地形。

intro.en: Terrain comes from French, from Latin terrenum 'earth, ground', built on terra. The Latin root is well attested. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: terrain 经法语来自拉丁语 terrenum「土地、地面」，由 terra 构成。拉丁词根书证充分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Terra meant 'earth, land, ground'. It goes back to a reconstructed root for dry land, seen also in territory and terrestrial.
items.cn: terra 意为「土地、陆地、地面」。它可上溯到一个表示干地的重构词根，亦见于 territory 与 terrestrial。

items.en: Terrenum meant 'earthly ground, land', the neuter form of terrenus 'of earth'.
items.cn: terrenum 意为「地上的土地」，是 terrenus「土地的」的中性形式。

items.en: French terrain carried the sense of ground considered for its surface and quality, especially in hunting and military writing.
items.cn: 法语 terrain 带有「就表面与性质而言的地面」之义，尤其见于狩猎与军事文献。

items.en: English borrowed terrain in the eighteenth century, chiefly in military and surveying contexts.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪借入 terrain，主要用于军事与测量语境。

items.en: Modeling, gaming, and recreation added new senses in the twentieth century; their first dates are not precisely recorded.
items.cn: 建模、游戏与休闲在 20 世纪增添新义，其最早年代没有精确记载。

note.en: Group one holds land-description words that are easily confused with terrain; group two holds words for land as property, surface, or setting.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 terrain 混淆的土地描述词；第二组是把土地视为财产、表面或环境的词。

entries.definition: An area under a state's control; it stresses ownership and boundaries rather than surface shape.
entries.definitionCN: 受国家控制的区域；强调所有权与边界，而非地表形状。

entries.definition: Relating to the earth or to land as opposed to water; it describes a realm, not a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 与地球或陆地（相对于水）有关；它描述领域，而非地表。

entries.definition: The Latin word for earth, used in scientific compounds such as terra incognita.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「土地」一词，用于 terra incognita 等学术短语。

entries.definition: The systematic description of surface features and elevations; terrain is the ground as experienced, topography as measured.
entries.definitionCN: 对地表特征与高程的系统描述；terrain 是体验到的地面，topography 是测量出的地形。

entries.definition: The visible appearance of an area, including vegetation and human features; it is what you see, not what you cross.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区的可见外观，包括植被与人工要素；它是你看到的，而非你穿越的。

entries.definition: The surface you stand on; it is neutral and lacks terrain's implication of difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 你站立其上的表面；它是中性的，不含 terrain 那种困难意味。

entries.definition: The difference in height across an area; it is one measurable property of terrain.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区内的高度差；它是地形的一项可测属性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin roots, real land terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁词根、真实土地术语与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Terrain and territory share Latin terra, but one is surface and the other is ownership.
normal.cn: terrain 与 territory 共享拉丁语 terra，但一个指表面，一个指所有权。

normal.en: Rough terrain is the standard phrase for ground that slows you down.
normal.cn: rough terrain 是描述拖慢行进的地面的标准短语。

normal.en: Terrain is what vehicles and troops must cross; landscape is what tourists photograph.
normal.cn: terrain 是车辆与部队要穿越的，landscape 是游客拍照的。

normal.en: A terrain map shows slope and elevation, not political borders.
normal.cn: 地形图显示坡度与高程，而非政治边界。

normal.en: The word entered English through French military vocabulary.
normal.cn: 这个词经法语军事词汇进入英语。

abstract.en: Picture a field of study with hills, swamps, and unmarked paths.
abstract.cn: 想象一个研究领域，里面有山丘、沼泽与没有标记的小路。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation whose ground shifts under every sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话，每说一句地面都在移动。

abstract.en: Picture a plan that looks easy on paper and turns to loose stone underfoot.
abstract.cn: 想象一个计划，纸上容易，脚下却变成松石。

examples.en: The jeep struggled over rough terrain full of loose stones.
examples.cn: 越野车在遍布松石的崎岖地形中艰难前行。

examples.en: The map shows terrain, water, and roads in separate colours.
examples.cn: 地图用不同颜色分别表示地形、水体与道路。

examples.en: The lizards survive only on rocky terrain with deep cracks.
examples.cn: 这些蜥蜴只在有深裂缝的岩石地形中存活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特雷恩」——车轮底下起伏不平的那片地 → 地形

root: 法语 terrain，来自拉丁语 terrenum「土地、地面」，由 terra「土地」构成；terra 可上溯到表示干地的重构印欧语词根，亦见于 territory 与 terrestrial。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow ground as surface, tract, obstacle, difficult country, model, habitat, metaphor, and recreation space.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让地面依次成为表面、地块、障碍、难行地带、模型、栖息地、比喻与休闲空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jeep pitching over loose stones on a steep, broken slope.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆越野车在陡峭破碎的坡面上被松石颠得起伏。

branches.en: SURFACE AND TRACT: the same ground is both a physical texture and a unit someone plans to use.
branches.cn: 表面与地块：同一片地既是物理质地，也是有人打算使用的单位。

branches.en: RESISTANCE: terrain becomes a technical word when the ground fights movement.
branches.cn: 阻力：当地面与移动对抗时，terrain 成为技术词。

branches.en: DATA: the land is reduced to elevation, slope, and texture in a model.
branches.cn: 数据：在模型中，土地被化简为高程、坡度与纹理。

branches.en: LIVING AND PLAYING: crevices are shelter for a lizard and features for a skier.
branches.cn: 生存与游玩：裂缝对蜥蜴是庇护所，对滑雪者则是地形特征。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any unfamiliar field can be crossed like rough country.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何陌生领域都能像崎岖地带一样被穿越。

intro.en: Terrain's family is built on Latin terra, one of the most productive land roots in English.
intro.cn: terrain 的词族建立在拉丁语 terra 上，这是英语中最多产的土地词根之一。

latinIntro.en: Latin terra and terrenum stand behind terrain; the same root gives territory, terrestrial, and terrace.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terra 与 terrenum 支撑 terrain；同一词根还给出 territory、terrestrial 与 terrace。

items.example: Terra is the root of many English land words.
items.exampleCN: terra 是许多英语土地词的词根。

items.example: Terrenum passed through French as terrain.
items.exampleCN: terrenum 经法语变为 terrain。

items.example: The terrain decides how fast a column can move.
items.exampleCN: 地形决定一队人马能走多快。

items.example: Territory stresses ownership, not slope.
items.exampleCN: territory 强调所有权，而非坡度。

items.example: Terrestrial animals cross terrain; aquatic ones do not.
items.exampleCN: 陆生动物穿越地形，水生动物则不。

items.structure: Old French terrace, from Latin terra
items.meaning: a raised flat platform of earth
items.example: Farmers cut terraces into the hillside terrain.
items.exampleCN: 农民在山坡地形上开出梯田。

items.meaningCN: 对地表的测量描述；地形学
items.example: Topography measures what terrain feels like.
items.exampleCN: 地形学测量 terrain 所感受到的东西。

items.example: Landscape is seen; terrain is crossed.
items.exampleCN: landscape 被看见，terrain 被穿越。

items.structure: Italian rilievo, from Latin relevare (to raise)
items.example: Relief is one property of terrain.
items.exampleCN: 起伏是地形的一项属性。

definition_zh: 陆地的；陆生的；地球的；陆栖的；类地的
definition_en: relating to the land or the earth, living on land rather than in water or in trees, or belonging to the planet Earth
core_image: 森林地面的苔藓间爬着甲虫，头顶是树冠，几步之外的溪水里另有生物
scene: 林下的苔藓和甲虫都生活在陆地上，与溪水里的生物全然不同。Mosses and beetles on the forest floor are terrestrial life, unlike the creatures in the stream.
sceneCN: 这里 terrestrial 指「生活在陆地上的」（第 1 个义项：陆生动物，与水生相对）；句意：林下的苔藓与甲虫是陆生生命，和溪水中的生物不同。图中可辨识物件：苔藓层、甲虫、落叶、几步外的溪流。

pos.zh: 陆地的；陆生的；地球的；陆栖的；类地的
陆地生物；地球人（少见，多用于科幻或生态分类）

derivatives.zh: 陆生动物饲养箱；玻璃花房

senses.title: Animals that live on land
senses.definition: describing animals that live mainly on dry land rather than in water
senses.definitionCN: 描述主要在干燥陆地上而非水中生活的动物
senses.example: Mosses and beetles on the forest floor are terrestrial life, unlike the creatures in the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 林下的苔藓与甲虫是陆生生命，和溪水中的生物不同。
senses.why: the Latin root terra means dry land, and ecology uses the adjective to mark the medium an animal occupies, contrasting it with aquatic.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 terra 意为干燥陆地，生态学用这个形容词标记动物所占的介质，与 aquatic 相对。

senses.title: Plants that grow on land
senses.definition: describing plants rooted in soil in the air rather than submerged or floating in water
senses.definitionCN: 描述扎根土壤、暴露在空气中，而非沉水或浮水的植物
senses.example: Terrestrial plants had to evolve a waxy cuticle to hold moisture.
senses.exampleCN: 陆生植物必须演化出蜡质角质层来保住水分。
senses.why: botany applies the same land-and-air label to plants, where the decisive contrast is with aquatic and epiphytic growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把同一个「陆地加空气」的标签用于植物，关键对照是水生与附生。

senses.title: Of the planet Earth
senses.definition: relating to the earth as a planet, especially in contrast with other worlds
senses.definitionCN: 与作为行星的地球有关，尤与其它世界相对
senses.example: Terrestrial life may be the only life in this solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 地球生命也许是这个太阳系里唯一的生命。
senses.why: the adjective moves from land to the whole globe when the comparison shifts from water to space.
senses.whyCN: 当比较对象从水变成太空时，这个形容词便从陆地扩展到整个地球。

senses.title: Land as opposed to sea
senses.definition: belonging to dry land as a physical realm, as in terrestrial transport or terrestrial borders
senses.definitionCN: 属于干燥陆地这一物理领域，如陆路运输、陆地边界
senses.example: The isthmus is the narrowest terrestrial link between the two seas.
senses.exampleCN: 这条地峡是两海之间最窄的陆上通道。
senses.why: this sense treats land as a surface for movement and boundaries, so terrestrial pairs with maritime and aerial.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把陆地看作通行与划界的表面，因此 terrestrial 与 maritime、aerial 构成系列。

senses.title: Rocky planets like Earth
senses.titleCN: 类地行星（以岩石为主的行星）
senses.definition: describing planets made mainly of rock and metal, with solid surfaces, rather than gas giants
senses.definitionCN: 描述主要由岩石与金属构成、有固体表面的行星，区别于气态巨行星
senses.example: Mars and Venus are the other terrestrial planets of the inner system.
senses.exampleCN: 火星与金星是内太阳系另外两颗类地行星。
senses.why: astronomy reuses the land word for bodies with a solid surface, since a rocky planet is land writ large.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把「陆地」一词用于有固体表面的天体，因为岩石行星就是放大的陆地。

senses.title: Ground-based broadcasting or networks
senses.titleCN: 地面（而非卫星）的广播与通信
senses.definition: describing communication systems based on land stations rather than satellites or cables
senses.definitionCN: 描述以陆地站点而非卫星或海底光缆为基础的通信系统
senses.example: Terrestrial broadcasting still reaches farms beyond the fibre network.
senses.exampleCN: 地面广播仍能覆盖光纤网络之外的农场。
senses.why: the sense extends land-based physical infrastructure to radio and television, where the ground station anchors the network.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把陆基实体设施扩展到广播电视，地面站是网络的锚点。

senses.title: Ground-dwelling rather than tree-dwelling
senses.definition: in ecology, describing species that forage or live on the ground rather than in the canopy
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指在地面觅食或栖息、而非在树冠层的物种
senses.example: The reserve protects both terrestrial and arboreal primates.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区同时保护地栖与树栖的灵长类。
senses.why: within land habitats the adjective is narrowed further: ground is the medium, and arboreal is its opposite.
senses.whyCN: 在陆地生境内部，这个形容词进一步收窄：地面是介质，树栖是它的对立面。

senses.title: Of land ecosystems as a category
senses.titleCN: 陆地生态系统的（与水域生态相对）
senses.definition: used for ecosystems, carbon pools and biodiversity found on land, as opposed to aquatic or marine ones
senses.definitionCN: 指陆地上的生态系统、碳库与生物多样性，与水生态或海洋生态相对
senses.example: Terrestrial carbon storage depends heavily on soil depth.
senses.exampleCN: 陆地碳储量在很大程度上取决于土壤深度。
senses.why: global-change science needs a cover term for all land systems, so terrestrial becomes the standard label for that pool.
senses.whyCN: 全球变化研究需要统称所有陆地系统，terrestrial 因而成为这一集合的标准标签。

intro.en: Terrestrial comes from Latin terrestris 'of the earth', built on terra 'dry land, earth' plus the suffix -estris. English adopted it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: terrestrial 来自拉丁 terrestris「大地的」，由 terra「干燥陆地、大地」加后缀 -estris 构成，16 世纪进入英语。

items.en: Terra meant 'dry land, earth, soil'. Its own origin is debated; a connection with a root meaning 'to dry' is often proposed but remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: terra 意为「干燥陆地、大地、土壤」。其自身来源有争议；常有人提出它与表示「干燥」的词根有关，但这仍是假说。

items.en: The adjective terrestris 'of the earth, earthly' was formed with -estris, and it contrasted with marine and celestial things.
items.cn: 形容词 terrestris「大地的、尘世的」由 -estris 构成，与海洋的、天界的事物相对。

items.en: English took terrestrial in the 1500s, first for earthly things in theology and then for land-dwelling creatures in natural history.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 terrestrial，最初在神学中指尘世之物，随后在博物学中指陆生生物。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word was applied to solid, earth-like planets, giving the modern term terrestrial planet.
items.cn: 19 世纪，该词被用于有固体表面、类似地球的行星，形成现代术语 terrestrial planet。

items.en: Twentieth-century engineering used terrestrial for ground-based stations and networks, in contrast with satellite systems.
items.cn: 20 世纪的工程用语用 terrestrial 指地面站点与网络，与卫星系统相对。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Latin history of terra is unsettled, so any Indo-European root given for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：terra 在拉丁语之前的历史无定论，凡为其给出的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates terrestrial from same-root words naming terrain, tanks and planets, and from one look-alike from a different root; group two contrasts it with habitat terms.
note.cn: 第一组把 terrestrial 与同根却指地形、饲养箱、行星的词区分开，并辨明一个词根不同的形近词；第二组对照栖息地词语。

entries.definition: The physical surface of an area of land; it descends from Latin terrenum 'earth', so it shares terra but names ground shape, not habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 指一片土地的物质表面；源自拉丁 terrenum「土地」，与 terra 同源，但指地面形态而非栖息环境。

entries.definition: A glass container for land plants or small land animals; the -arium suffix makes it a place, not an adjective of habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 养陆生植物或小动物的玻璃容器；-arium 后缀使它指场所，而非栖息地形容词。

entries.definition: A crustal block with a geological history distinct from its neighbours; it is a technical geology term from the same terra stock.
entries.definitionCN: 地质历史与邻区不同的地壳块体；是同一 terra 词族的地质学专门术语。

entries.definition: Very good or very intense; it comes from Latin terrere 'to frighten', not terra 'earth', so the resemblance is deceptive.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的或极强烈的；来自拉丁 terrere「使害怕」而非 terra「大地」，因此形近而不同源。

entries.definition: Living or growing in water; it is the direct opposite of terrestrial in ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 在水中生活或生长的；生态学中与 terrestrial 直接相对。

entries.definition: Living in trees; it narrows the land habitat further and contrasts with ground-dwelling terrestrial species.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在树上的；它把陆地生境进一步收窄，与地栖的陆生物种相对。

entries.definition: Relating to a continent or to the interior of one; it names scale, while terrestrial names the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 与大陆或大陆内部有关的；它命名尺度，而 terrestrial 命名介质。

entries.definition: Belonging to this world rather than heaven; it is the theological and poetic cousin of terrestrial.
entries.definitionCN: 属于今生此世而非天界的；是 terrestrial 在神学与诗歌中的近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real terra root, real compounds and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 terra 词根、真实复合词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Terra is Latin for earth, and it also gives terrain, terrarium, territory and Mediterranean.
normal.cn: terra 是拉丁语的「大地」，也构成 terrain、terrarium、territory 与 Mediterranean。

normal.en: The fixed ecology pair is terrestrial / aquatic, dividing habitats by medium.
normal.cn: 生态学的固定配对是 terrestrial / aquatic，按介质划分生境。

normal.en: Extraterrestrial adds extra- 'outside' to the same adjective, so it means 'outside the earth'.
normal.cn: extraterrestrial 在同一形容词前加 extra-「之外」，意为「地球之外的」。

normal.en: Terrestrial planets are the rocky four: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
normal.cn: 类地行星是四颗岩石行星：水星、金星、地球与火星。

normal.en: Subterranean puts sub- 'under' before the same terra stock, meaning 'under the earth'.
normal.cn: subterranean 在同一 terra 词族前加 sub-「在下」，意为「地下的」。

abstract.en: Picture a beetle that never touches water and a fish that never touches soil, each complete in its own element.
abstract.cn: 想象一只从不沾水的甲虫与一条从不沾土的鱼，各自在自己的元素里完整无缺。

abstract.en: Picture a globe small enough to hold, with dry land painted on it as a single colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一个可以捧在手里的地球仪，干燥陆地被涂成同一种颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a radio mast rooted in soil while a satellite floats above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根扎在土里的广播天线，而卫星在它上方漂浮。

examples.en: Terrestrial animals must conserve water in dry seasons.
examples.cn: 陆生动物在旱季必须节约用水。

examples.en: The telescope search focuses on terrestrial planets in nearby systems.
examples.cn: 这台望远镜的搜寻聚焦于邻近星系中的类地行星。

examples.en: Terrestrial carbon pools respond slowly to changes in land use.
examples.cn: 陆地碳库对土地利用变化的反应很慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「terra（土地）+ e（的）」——terra 是土地，terrestrial 就是「属于土地的」

root: 拉丁 terrestris「大地的」= terra「干燥陆地、大地」+ -estris（形容词后缀）；terra 的更深来源不确定，与「干燥」词根的联系仅为假说。英语 terrestrial。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move outward from soil: animals, plants, the whole planet, land as opposed to sea, rocky planets, ground-based networks, the ground layer of a forest, and land ecosystems as a global category.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从土壤向外扩展：动物、植物、整个行星、与海相对的陆地、岩石行星、地面网络、森林的地面层，以及作为全球类别的陆地生态系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life and structures rooted in dry ground rather than water.
core.cn: 核心意象：扎根于干燥陆地而非水中的生命与设施。

branches.en: LAND-DWELLING LIFE: animals and plants are classified by the ground they occupy.
branches.cn: 陆生生命：动物与植物按所占地面被分类。

branches.en: LAND AS A REALM: the adjective widens from soil to the whole planet and to land transport.
branches.cn: 陆地领域：形容词从土壤扩展到整个行星与陆路运输。

branches.en: SOLID WORLDS: a rocky planet is land written at planetary scale.
branches.cn: 固体世界：岩石行星就是行星尺度的陆地。

branches.en: GROUND INFRASTRUCTURE: stations on land anchor broadcast networks.
branches.cn: 地面设施：陆地站点锚定广播网络。

branches.en: ECOLOGICAL DIVISIONS: ground versus canopy inside land, and land versus water globally.
branches.cn: 生态划分：陆地内部地面与树冠相对，全球范围内陆地与水相对。

intro.en: Terrestrial is a Latin adjective from terra, and that root also supports terrain, territory, terrarium and subterranean, while extra- builds its best-known opposite.
intro.cn: terrestrial 是由 terra 构成的拉丁形容词，这个词根还支撑 terrain、territory、terrarium 与 subterranean，而 extra- 构成它最知名的反义词。

latinIntro.en: Latin terra 'earth' and terrestris 'of the earth' are the direct ancestors; terrenus 'earthy' belongs to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 terra「大地」与 terrestris「大地的」是直接祖形；terrenus「土质的」属于同一词族。

items.example: Terra appears in many scientific compound terms.
items.exampleCN: terra 出现在许多科学复合术语中。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the nature of
items.example: Terrestris means of the earth.
items.exampleCN: terrestris 意为大地的。

items.example: The terrestrial habitat lies above the tideline.
items.exampleCN: 陆生栖息地位于潮线之上。

items.example: The probe listens for extraterrestrial signals.
items.exampleCN: 探测器监听外星信号。

items.example: The terrain rises sharply east of the river.
items.exampleCN: 河以东的地势陡然升高。

items.example: The terrarium mimics a damp forest floor.
items.exampleCN: 饲养箱模拟湿润的森林地面。

items.example: The terrane drifted in from another plate.
items.exampleCN: 这块地体从另一板块漂移而来。

items.example: Subterranean rivers cut through the limestone.
items.exampleCN: 地下河切穿石灰岩。

items.example: The wolves defend a fixed territory.
items.exampleCN: 狼群守卫固定的领地。

definition_zh: 领土；地盘；（动物的）领域；领域；地区
definition_en: an area of land under a particular authority, or an area that an animal, person, or group treats as its own
core_image: 一只动物沿着灌木丛嗅出一圈界线，把这片地划成自己的
scene: 两只狼在河谷边缘留下气味标记，警告外来者不要进入这片领地。 Two wolves left scent marks along the edge of the valley, warning outsiders not to enter their territory.
sceneCN: 这里 territory 是「（动物的）领域、地盘」（第 2 个义项：动物防卫的空间）；句意：两只狼在河谷边缘留下气味标记，警告外来者不要进入这片领地。

pos.zh: 领土；属地；地区；领域；地盘（可数，复数为 territories）

derivatives.zh: 领土的；地盘的；区域性的
领域性；地盘意识；属地原则

senses.title: Land under a state's authority
senses.definition: the land and waters under the legal authority of a state or government
senses.definitionCN: 处于国家或政府法律管辖之下的陆地与水域
senses.example: The treaty fixed the northern territory of the two nations.
senses.exampleCN: 条约确定了两国的北部领土。
senses.why: Latin territorium first meant the land around a town, from terra 'earth'. The political sense grew by extending that 'land belonging to a centre' to a whole state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 territorium 最初指“城镇周围的土地”，来自 terra「土地」。政治义是把“属于某一中心的土地”扩展到整个国家。

senses.title: An animal's defended area
senses.definition: the area an animal or group defends against intruders of the same or other species
senses.definitionCN: 动物或群体防御同种或其他物种入侵的空间
senses.example: The male warbler sings at dawn to advertise his territory.
senses.exampleCN: 雄莺在黎明鸣唱以宣告自己的领域。
senses.why: The political notion of bounded land is applied to behaviour: a bird treats a patch as if it were owned, and trespass is met with song or attack.
senses.whyCN: “有边界的土地”这一政治概念被用于行为：鸟把一块地当作己有，入侵者会遭到鸣唱警告或攻击。

senses.title: A field of knowledge or activity
senses.definition: a domain of study, expertise, or action that belongs to a group or discipline
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一群体或学科的研究、专长或行动范围
senses.example: Genetic editing lies in territory that older regulations never covered.
senses.exampleCN: 基因编辑属于旧法规从未覆盖的领域。
senses.why: The spatial metaphor shifts from soil to concepts: an area is 'held' by a discipline just as land is held by a state, so new work is either inside or outside that boundary.
senses.whyCN: 空间隐喻从土地转向概念：一个学科“持有”某个区域，就像国家持有土地，因此新研究要么在边界内，要么在边界外。

senses.title: Commercial or sales area
senses.definition: a region assigned to a salesperson, branch, or company as its exclusive market
senses.definitionCN: 分配给销售员、分支机构或公司的专属市场区域
senses.example: The firm split the coast into three sales territories.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把沿海地区分成三个销售区域。
senses.why: Modern business reuses the oldest structure: a centre assigns a bounded patch to an agent, and the boundary is protected against rival sellers.
senses.whyCN: 现代商业复用了最古老的结构：中心把一块有边界的区域分给代理人，并防御竞争对手进入。

senses.title: A region or district
senses.definition: a general region of land, especially one with a distinguishing feature or administration
senses.definitionCN: 具有某种特征或行政建制的广大地带
senses.example: Mountain territory covers most of the province.
senses.exampleCN: 山区地带占该省的大部分。
senses.why: The word often simply names land at a regional scale, without the strict legal or behavioural sense; the boundary is geographic rather than defended.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常只指区域尺度的土地，不带严格的法律或行为含义；边界是地理性的，而非被防卫的。

senses.title: A dependent possession
senses.definition: a land governed by another country but not fully integrated into it
senses.definitionCN: 由另一国治理但未完全并入该国的土地
senses.example: The islands remain a territory of the mainland state.
senses.exampleCN: 这些岛屿仍是大陆国家的属地。
senses.why: Imperial and colonial usage made territory the word for land held from outside; the people there may have rights of residence without full citizenship.
senses.whyCN: 帝国与殖民用法使 territory 成为“从外部持有的土地”的用词；当地居民可能拥有居住权而无法获得完整公民身份。

senses.title: Unfamiliar or dangerous ground
senses.definition: in figurative use, a situation or subject that people have not dealt with before
senses.definitionCN: 用于比喻，指人们此前未曾应对过的处境或主题
senses.example: Negotiating with the rebels took the envoys into unknown territory.
senses.exampleCN: 与叛军谈判把使节带入了未知领域。
senses.why: The metaphor treats experience as a map: known land is charted, unknown land is territory without marks, and entering it means risk.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把经验当作地图：已知之地被测绘，未知之地是没有标记的 territory，进入它就意味着风险。

senses.title: A marked area in a game or sport
senses.titleCN: 比赛或运动中的场地范围
senses.definition: the part of a playing field or board assigned to a player or team
senses.definitionCN: 运动场或棋盘上分配给某一方或队员的区域
senses.example: The defender refused to leave his territory near the goal.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫拒绝离开球门附近的防区。
senses.why: Games formalize the same instinct: space is divided and each player is responsible for one patch, so 'territory' becomes a rule rather than a claim.
senses.whyCN: 比赛把同一种本能形式化：空间被划分，每名球员负责一块区域，于是 territory 成为规则而不是主张。

intro.en: Territory came from Latin territorium, the land around a town. Its link to terra 'land' is clear, but a popular derivation from terrere 'to frighten' remains disputed, so that branch is marked uncertain.
intro.cn: territory 来自拉丁语 territorium，即城镇周围的土地。它与 terra「土地」的联系清楚，但流行的“来自 terrere「使恐惧」”一说仍有争议，故该分支标注为不确定。

items.en: English territory is recorded in the late fourteenth century meaning 'land under the jurisdiction of a town or lord'.
items.cn: 英语 territory 于 14 世纪晚期被记录，义为“城镇或领主管辖下的土地”。

items.en: From Latin territorium 'land around a town, domain, district'. The suffix -orium marks a place associated with something.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 territorium「城镇周围的土地、领地、区域」。后缀 -orium 标记与某物相关的地点。

items.en: The base is terra 'earth, land', which also gives terrain, terrace, Mediterranean and terracotta. This part of the history is well supported.
items.cn: 词基是 terra「土地」，还衍生 terrain、terrace、Mediterranean、terracotta。这部分历史有充分支持。

items.en: Some sources connect territorium with terrere 'to frighten' and territare 'to frighten repeatedly', which would make the original sense 'land kept by fear'. Standard references disagree, so this link is source uncertain.
items.cn: 有些资料把 territorium 与 terrere「使恐惧」、territare「反复恐吓」联系起来，那样原义会是“靠恐惧守住的土地”。通行资料并不一致，故该联系来源不确定。

items.en: The sense widened to colonial possessions and to figurative 'field of knowledge'; in the 20th century ethology borrowed it for defended animal space.
items.cn: 词义扩展到殖民地属地与比喻性的“知识领域”；20 世纪动物行为学又借它指被防卫的动物空间。

items.en: Modern English keeps the political, behavioural, commercial, and figurative senses side by side; the plural territories is standard.
items.cn: 现代英语并列保留政治、行为、商业与比喻义；复数 territories 为标准形式。

note.en: The first group separates form neighbours, the second compares words for land and defended space.
note.cn: 第一组区分词形相近者，第二组比较表示土地与防卫空间的词。

entries.definition: the physical surface of land, its slope and texture. It is ground as landscape, not ground as jurisdiction.
entries.definitionCN: 土地的地表形态、坡度与质地。它是作为景观的地面，而非作为管辖范围的地面。

entries.definition: a flat raised strip of land; from terra through French. It shares the earth base but not the political sense.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦的台地；经法语来自 terra。共享“土地”词基，但无政治义。

entries.definition: extreme fear, from terrere 'to frighten'. It is not a relative unless the disputed territory link is accepted.
entries.definitionCN: 极度恐惧，来自 terrere「使恐惧」。除非接受有争议的 territory 联系，否则并非同源。

entries.definition: relating to territory; also the adjective for defensive behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 与领土有关的；也指防卫行为的形容词。

entries.definition: an area owned or controlled, often legal or feudal; also a field of expertise. It is more formal than territory.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有或控制的区域，常为法律或封建语境；也指专长领域。比 territory 更正式。

entries.definition: a broad area defined by geography or administration. It lacks the sense of defence or ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 由地理或行政界定的大片区域。缺少防卫或占有之义。

entries.definition: the area in which a species occurs. It is not necessarily defended.
entries.definitionCN: 物种出现的区域。不一定被防卫。

entries.definition: the surface or an area underfoot, or a field of argument. It is neutral and physical.
entries.definitionCN: 脚下的地面或场地，也指论点领域。中性且偏物理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, standard phrases, and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语成分、标准搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: terra means earth: territory is land marked off as belonging to someone.
normal.cn: terra 意为土地：territory 是被划出来、属于某人的土地。

normal.en: Mark its territory is the fixed phrase for animals leaving scent, sound, or visible signs.
normal.cn: mark its territory 是动物留下气味、声音或可见标记的固定说法。

normal.en: Terrain is the same land seen as surface; territory is the same land seen as ownership.
normal.cn: terrain 是把同一片土地看作地表；territory 是把同一片土地看作所有权。

normal.en: Sales territory shows how ordinary the structure is: a company assigns a patch to a seller.
normal.cn: sales territory 说明这个结构多么日常：公司把一块区域分给销售员。

normal.en: Unknown territory is the figurative branch: experience drawn as a map with blank areas.
normal.cn: unknown territory 是比喻分支：把经验画成一张留有空白的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn in grass: on one side is 'mine', on the other 'not mine'. Territory is the area inside the line, however the line is made.
abstract.cn: 想象在草地上画一条线：一边是“我的”，另一边是“不是我的”。territory 就是线内的区域，无论线是怎么画出来的。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from states to animals to disciplines to sales because all four involve a centre assigning and defending a bounded area.
abstract.cn: 这个词能轻易从国家转到动物、学科、销售，因为四者都涉及一个中心分配并防卫有边界的区域。

abstract.en: Behavioral territory is not property in law; it is a claim enforced by presence, not by title.
abstract.cn: 行为学上的领域不是法律财产；它是由在场维系的 claim，而不是由产权证维系。

examples.en: The river forms the eastern boundary of the territory.
examples.cn: 这条河构成该领土的东部边界。

examples.en: Robins defend their territory against intruders throughout the spring.
examples.cn: 整个春天，知更鸟都在防御领地、抵御入侵者。

examples.en: The question of consciousness is still unexplored territory for the lab.
examples.cn: 意识问题对该实验室仍是未探索的领域。

dict_mnemonic.text: “太弱的里”——这片地里太弱的人守不住，只能让强敌占去 → territory 领地、领土

root: 拉丁语 territorium「城镇周围的土地」，词基 terra「土地」；与 terrere「使恐惧」的联系存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of territory: a bounded area held by a state, an animal, a discipline, a company, a game, or the imagination. The common core is 'land marked as belonging'.
sensesIntro.cn: territory 的八个义项：由国家、动物、学科、公司、比赛或想象持有的有边界区域。共同核心是“被标记为属于某方的土地”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn around a patch of ground, with 'mine' inside and 'not mine' outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一片土地周围画一条线，线内是“我的”，线外是“不是我的”。

branches.en: POLITICS: land under a state, including dependent possessions beyond the core.
branches.cn: 政治：国家管辖的土地，包括核心之外的属地。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR AND PLAY: animals and players defend an assigned patch.
branches.cn: 行为与比赛：动物与球员防卫被分配的区域。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: a discipline's field, or the blank part of the map called unknown.
branches.cn: 知识：学科领域，或被称作“未知”的地图空白部分。

branches.en: COMMERCE: a company assigns a market patch to an agent.
branches.cn: 商业：公司把一块市场区域分给代理人。

branches.en: GEOGRAPHY: a broad region named by its features rather than by defence.
branches.cn: 地理：以特征而非防卫命名的广大地区。

intro.en: Territory is a Latin noun in -orium, a suffix of place. English adds the adjective and noun suffixes -ial and -iality, but does not build the root anew.
intro.cn: territory 是带 -orium（地点后缀）的拉丁名词。英语只加形容词与名词后缀 -ial、-iality，并不重新构造词根。

latinIntro.en: Terra 'earth' yields terrain, terrace, terracotta, and Mediterranean; the territorium branch yields territorial, territoriality, and the verb territorialize.
latinIntro.cn: terra「土地」衍生 terrain、terrace、terracotta、Mediterranean；territorium 这一支衍生 territorial、territoriality 与动词 territorialize。

items.meaningCN: 领土的；领域的（-ial 形容词）
items.example: Territorial claims caused the war.
items.exampleCN: 领土主张引发了战争。

items.meaning: the state or practice of holding territory
items.meaningCN: 领域性；属地状态（-ity 名词）
items.example: Territoriality is common in songbirds.
items.exampleCN: 领域性在鸣禽中很常见。

items.meaning: to make into or organize by territory
items.meaningCN: 使领土化；按区域组织（-ize 动词）
items.example: States territorialize maritime space.
items.exampleCN: 国家把海洋空间领土化。

items.meaningCN: 在领土或地域方面（-ly 副词）
items.example: The region is territorially divided.
items.exampleCN: 该地区在地域上被划分。

items.example: The terrain is too steep for trucks.
items.exampleCN: 地形太陡，卡车无法通行。

items.meaning: a flat raised shelf of land
items.example: Rice grows on the terraces.
items.exampleCN: 水稻种在梯田上。

items.example: The roof tiles are terracotta.
items.exampleCN: 屋顶瓦片是红陶的。

items.meaning: the sea in the middle of land
items.example: Olives grow across the Mediterranean.
items.exampleCN: 橄榄树遍布地中海地区。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 使恐惧（与 territory 的联系存疑）

definition_zh: 恐怖；恐惧；可怕的人或事物；恐怖行动
definition_en: a feeling of extreme fear, the use of violence to frighten people, or a person or thing that causes great fear
core_image: 深夜空巷里身后逼近的脚步声：心跳到喉咙口的那种怕
scene: 停电的楼道一片漆黑，身后传来急促的脚步声。She froze in terror as the footsteps came closer.
sceneCN: 这里 terror 是「极度恐惧」（第 1 个义项：强烈的恐惧感）；句意：脚步声逼近，她吓得僵在原地。

pos.zh: 恐怖；恐惧；可怕的人或事；恐怖行动

collocations.zh: 班里的捣蛋鬼；令人生畏者

derivatives.zh: 恐怖分子（由 terror 加表人后缀 -ist 构成，指实施恐怖活动的人）
使恐惧；使害怕（由 terror 加动词后缀派生，义为把恐惧灌进人心）
令人恐惧的（terrify 的现在分词转形容词）
吓坏了的（terrify 的过去分词转形容词）

senses.title: Extreme fear
senses.definition: the state of feeling extreme and overwhelming fear
senses.definitionCN: 感到强烈而压倒性的恐惧的状态
senses.example: The villagers fled in terror when the flood came.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水来时村民惊恐地逃散。
senses.why: The word names fear at its highest pitch, when the body reacts before the mind can decide.
senses.whyCN: 它命名的是恐惧的最高强度：身体先于头脑作出反应的那一瞬。

senses.title: Violence used to frighten people
senses.titleCN: 恐怖行径：以暴力制造恐慌
senses.definition: the deliberate use of violence and fear to control people
senses.definitionCN: 刻意使用暴力与恐惧来控制人群
senses.example: The dictator ruled the country by a campaign of terror.
senses.exampleCN: 独裁者靠恐怖统治控制这个国家。
senses.why: Fear can be weaponized: when fright is produced on purpose, the feeling itself becomes a method of ruling.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧可以被武器化：当恐惧被刻意制造，这种感觉本身就变成了统治手段。

senses.title: A person or thing that causes fear
senses.definition: a person or thing that frightens others greatly
senses.definitionCN: 让别人非常害怕的人或事物
senses.example: Her elder brother is a terror behind the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 她哥哥开车是个马路杀手。
senses.why: Whatever reliably produces the feeling can be called by it: the cause borrows the name of the effect.
senses.whyCN: 凡是可靠地制造恐惧的东西都可以借用它的名字：原因借走了结果的名称。

senses.title: A frightening or troublesome child
senses.definition: a child who behaves badly and is difficult to handle, often said with affection
senses.definitionCN: 胡闹难管的孩子，常带亲昵口吻
senses.example: Young Tommy is a little terror at the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 小汤米在饭桌上是个小捣蛋。
senses.why: The effect produced is chaos rather than fear, but the fixed phrase keeps the name, softened by smiles.
senses.whyCN: 制造的效果是混乱而非害怕，但固定短语保留了这个名字，且被笑意软化了。

intro.en: Terror is a Latin loan: the noun terrere meant to frighten, and terror was the fright itself. English took the word through French and never lost the ancient image.
intro.cn: terror 是拉丁语借词：动词 terrere 意为「吓」，名词 terror 就是那股吓意。英语经法语接收了这个词，古老的意象从未丢失。

items.en: The Latin verb terrere meant to frighten or make tremble, and terror named the state of being frightened.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 terrere 意为惊吓、使人发抖，名词 terror 指被吓住的状态。

items.en: The root tremble-image links terror to the idea that real fear shakes the body visibly.
items.cn: 词根的「发抖」意象把 terror 与「真正的恐惧会看得见地摇动身体」联系在一起。

items.en: French carried terreur into medieval and early modern writing, keeping both private dread and public violence.
items.cn: 法语把 terreur 带进中世纪与近代早期的文字，既有私人的惧怕，也有公共的暴力。

items.en: English borrowed terror in the late Middle Ages, at first for religious dread and bodily shaking before God.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入 terror，最初用于宗教性的敬畏与在神面前发抖。

items.en: The Reign of Terror in the 1790s fixed the political sense, and later everyday use softened it to pranks and mischievous children.
items.cn: 1790 年代的恐怖统治固定了政治义；此后日常用法又把它软化，用来称呼恶作剧的孩子。

note.en: Terror sits beside its own verb and agent, and beside fear words of different strength.
note.cn: terror 与它自己的动词、施动者并列，也与强度不同的恐惧类词并列。

entries.definition: to fill someone with great fear; the verb form of the terror family
entries.definitionCN: 使人大为恐惧；terror 词族的动词形式

entries.definition: originally frightening, now excellent; the old sense of terror survives only in the spelling
entries.definitionCN: 原义吓人，今义极好；terror 的古义只残留在拼写里

entries.definition: a small hunting dog; only looks close to terror, etymology is different
entries.definitionCN: 一种小型猎犬；只是拼写接近 terror，词源不同

entries.definition: fear mixed with anticipation, a slower and heavier feeling than terror
entries.definitionCN: 带着预期的恐惧，比 terror 更慢更沉

entries.definition: sudden wild fear that spreads in a crowd and destroys self-control
entries.definitionCN: 人群中蔓延、让人失去自控的突发恐慌

entries.definition: fear mixed with disgust or shock at something repulsive
entries.definitionCN: 恐惧中混着厌恶或震惊；对可怖之物的反应

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Latin verb terrere, the terrify family, the Reign of Terror, and the schoolroom little terror.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁动词 terrere、terrify 词族、恐怖统治、以及教室里的小捣蛋。

normal.en: Terrere in Latin means to make someone tremble; terror is fear that shakes the body.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 terrere 意为使人发抖；terror 就是会摇动身体的恐惧。

normal.en: Terrify, terrified and terrifying all carry the same root into verbs and adjectives.
normal.cn: terrify、terrified、terrifying 把同一词根带进动词与形容词。

normal.en: The Reign of Terror in history fixed the sense of violence used as government.
normal.cn: 历史上的恐怖统治固定了「以暴力为统治」的义项。

normal.en: Strike terror into the enemy: aim the fear like an arrow.
normal.cn: strike terror into the enemy：像箭一样把恐惧射进敌心。

normal.en: A little terror at home frightens nobody; the phrase only borrows the word for mischief.
normal.cn: 家里的「小 terror」谁也吓不倒；短语只是借这个词来称呼淘气。

abstract.en: Terror is the moment the body votes before the mind has finished counting.
abstract.cn: terror 是身体在头脑尚未数完票之前就先投票的那一刻。

abstract.en: Fear as a tool of power turns a feeling into a wall.
abstract.cn: 被当作权力的工具时，恐惧就成了一堵墙。

abstract.en: A shaking hand can be afraid, and can also be the thing that frightens others.
abstract.cn: 发抖的手可以是在害怕，也可以正是吓坏别人的东西。

examples.en: She fled the burning house in terror.
examples.cn: 她惊恐地逃离着火的房子。

examples.en: The bomb exploded with a terror that nobody in the street had known before.
examples.cn: 炸弹爆炸带来街上无人经历过的恐怖。

examples.en: Visiting the dentist terrified him as a child.
examples.cn: 小时候看牙医吓坏了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太怕」——太怕了，腿直发抖 → terror 恐怖、恐惧

root: 拉丁语 terrere「惊吓、使发抖」→ 拉丁名词 terror「恐惧」→ 经法语进入英语；terrify、terrific、terrier 一带词形相近但义路各异。

sensesIntro.en: Terror begins as pure fear at its strongest, then stretches into fear as a weapon, the frightful cause itself, and finally the smiling sense of a mischievous child.
sensesIntro.cn: terror 从最高强度的恐惧出发，延伸为作为武器的恐惧、可怕的原因本身，最后软化为淘气孩子的昵称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fear so strong the body trembles before the mind decides.
core.cn: 核心意象：强烈到身体先于头脑发抖的恐惧。

branches.en: The feeling at its highest pitch.
branches.cn: 恐惧的最高强度。

branches.en: Fear produced on purpose becomes a method of control.
branches.cn: 被刻意制造的恐惧成为统治手段。

branches.en: The cause borrows the name of the feeling it creates.
branches.cn: 原因借走它所制造的 feelings 的名称。

branches.en: Everyday speech softens the word to playful mischief.
branches.cn: 日常口语把这个词软化成顽皮的昵称。

branches.en: Private trembling and public violence are one root apart.
branches.cn: 私人的发抖与公共的暴力只隔一个词根。

intro.en: Terror builds its family with the agent suffix -ist, the verb suffixes -ify and -able, and the noun suffix -ism.
intro.cn: terror 用表人后缀 -ist、动词后缀 -ify 与 -able、名词后缀 -ism 构建词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gave English terror directly; terrere is also the source of terrific and the French-derived detour behind deter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语直接把 terror 交给英语；terrere 同样派生 terrific，也绕经法语造出 deter。

items.meaning: a person who uses terror as a political weapon
items.meaningCN: 以恐怖为政治武器的人
items.example: The terrorist group claimed the attack.
items.exampleCN: 恐怖组织宣称对袭击负责。

items.meaning: to fill someone with great fear
items.example: The horror film terrified the children.
items.exampleCN: 恐怖片吓坏了孩子们。

items.example: a terrifying noise in the dark
items.exampleCN: 黑暗中可怕的声音

items.example: He was terrified of dogs.
items.exampleCN: 他非常怕狗。

items.meaning: to control people by repeated terror
items.meaningCN: 以持续的恐怖手段控制
items.example: The gang terrorized the whole street.
items.exampleCN: 这伙匪帮恐吓了整条街的人。

items.example: High fines deter careless drivers.
items.exampleCN: 高额罚款让粗心的司机却步。

items.example: The alarm is a good deterrent to thieves.
items.exampleCN: 警报器是很好的防盗威慑。

items.meaning: a small secret group of terrorists
items.example: Police broke up a terror cell in the port.
items.exampleCN: 警方捣毁了港口的一个恐怖小组。

items.meaning: a glass case for growing plants
items.example: The school keeps a terrarium of ferns.
items.exampleCN: 学校养着一缸蕨类。

definition_zh: 作证；证实；（事物）表明、证明
definition_en: to give evidence in a court of law, or to show clearly that something is true
core_image: 手按誓词，把看到的那一幕原样说出来
scene: 法庭上，一名修理工把当天看到的火情按时间顺序讲给法官听。The mechanic must testify that the alarm had failed twice that month.
sceneCN: 这里 testify 指出庭给出证词（第 1 个义项：以证人身份在法庭上陈述）；句意为修理工作证说那个月警报器两次失灵。图中可辨识物件：证人席、工作服、警报器照片、法官的记录本。

pos.zh: 作证；提供证词
证实；表明；证明

derivatives.zh: 证明；证实（同出 testari 词根）

senses.title: Give evidence on the stand
senses.definition: to give evidence as a witness in a court
senses.definitionCN: 作为证人在法庭上提供证据
senses.example: The mechanic testified that the alarm had failed twice that month.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工作证说那个月警报器两次失灵。
senses.why: Testify is testis 'witness' plus -fy 'to make': the verb makes a person into a witness who speaks.
senses.whyCN: testify 是 testis「证人」加 -fy「使……成为」：这个动词把人变成开口的证人。

senses.title: State what one knows
senses.definition: to state in evidence what one saw, heard or knows
senses.definitionCN: 就所见、所闻或所知作出陈述
senses.example: Two neighbours testified that the lights were on all night.
senses.exampleCN: 两位邻居作证说整夜都亮着灯。
senses.why: The that-clause carries the content of the witness box into the record.
senses.whyCN: 这一从句结构把证人席上说出的内容带进案卷。

senses.title: Speak against someone
senses.definition: to give evidence that counts against an accused person
senses.definitionCN: 提供对被指控者不利的证据
senses.example: A former partner agreed to testify against the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 一名前合伙人同意作证指控这家公司。
senses.why: The preposition against turns the witness into an opposing party in the case.
senses.whyCN: 表示「反对」的介词把证人变成案件中的对立一方。

senses.title: Speak for someone
senses.definition: to give evidence in support of an accused person
senses.definitionCN: 提供对被指控者有利的证据
senses.example: His foreman testified for him at the sentencing hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 他的工头在量刑听证上为他作证。
senses.why: The same verb serves both sides; the preposition alone decides whose case is helped.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词对双方都适用，只由介词决定帮助哪一方。

senses.title: Things that bear witness
senses.definition: to show clearly that something is true, said of things rather than people
senses.definitionCN: 清楚表明某事为真，主语多为事物而非人
senses.example: The cracked foundations testify to years of subsidence.
senses.exampleCN: 开裂的地基证明多年下沉。
senses.why: Objects can testify in the same sense that a witness does: they make a fact evident to anyone who looks.
senses.whyCN: 物品「作证」与证人作证同理：它们让任何观看者都看清某项事实。

senses.title: Speak of faith in public
senses.titleCN: 宗教集会中公开讲述信仰
senses.definition: to give a personal account of religious experience to a group
senses.definitionCN: 在群体面前讲述个人的宗教经历
senses.example: She testified at the Wednesday meeting for the first time.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一次在周三聚会上讲述了自己的信仰经历。
senses.why: A congregation asks for the same formal personal account that a court asks of a witness.
senses.whyCN: 会众要求的，与法庭要求于证人的一样，都是正式的个人陈述。

senses.title: Address a hearing
senses.titleCN: 在听证会或委员会提供证言
senses.definition: to give formal evidence to a committee, commission or inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 向委员会、调查组或听证会提供正式证言
senses.example: The engineer testified before the transport committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这名工程师在交通委员会上作了证。
senses.why: The verb follows the witness wherever a formal record is being made.
senses.whyCN: 凡是要留下正式记录的地方，这个动词都跟着证人走。

senses.title: Establish by testimony
senses.definition: to establish or confirm something by giving evidence about it
senses.definitionCN: 通过提供相关证据来确立或确认某事
senses.example: The archivist testified to the authenticity of the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 档案管理员作证确认这封信的真实性。
senses.why: The preposition to marks what the evidence is meant to establish, not merely what was seen.
senses.whyCN: 表示「指向」的介词标出证据所要确立的东西，而不只是看见的内容。

intro.en: Testify comes through Old French testifier from Latin testificari 'to bear witness', built on testis 'witness' and facere 'to make'. It is recorded in English from the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: testify 经古法语 testifier 来自拉丁 testificari「作证」，由 testis「证人」与 facere「做、使」构成，十四世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Testis meant 'witness'; its deeper origin is not established, and the 'third person standing by' explanation is a reconstruction.
items.cn: testis 意为「证人」；其更深来源未获证明，「站在一旁的第三人」这一解释属于重构。

items.en: Testis plus facere produced testificari 'to bear witness, to call to witness'.
items.cn: testis 加 facere 构成 testificari「作证、传唤作证」。

items.en: Old French testifier carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 testifier 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.en: The earliest English use is legal: the verb describes a witness speaking in a case.
items.cn: 英语最早的用法属于法律：这个动词描述证人在案件中陈述。

items.en: By the sixteenth century objects and documents could testify as well, and the preposition to marked what they established.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，物品与文件也能「作证」，而表示「指向」的介词则标出它们所确立的内容。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of testis is a reconstruction, and the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：testis 在拉丁语之前的历史属于重构，最早书证的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same testari stock, including two built with different prefixes; group two holds verbs of swearing and affirming.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 testari 词干的词，其中两个由不同前缀构成；第二组是宣誓与确认类动词。

entries.definition: From testari in its will-making sense: a document that declares what happens after death.
entries.definitionCN: 取自 testari 的立遗嘱义：声明身后安排的文件。

entries.definition: A written statement praising a person's character or work, not evidence given in court.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞某人品行或工作表现的书面材料，不是庭上提供的证据。

entries.definition: Con- plus testari 'call to witness': to call witnesses together, hence to dispute or compete.
entries.definitionCN: con- 加 testari「传唤证人」：把证人一起叫来，因此指争辩或竞赛。

entries.definition: Pro- plus testari: to declare openly before witnesses, hence to object publicly.
entries.definitionCN: pro- 加 testari：在证人面前公开声明，因此指公开反对。

entries.definition: To confirm that something is true, often by signature or by evidence rather than by a court appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 确认某事为真，多凭签名或证据，而非出庭。

entries.definition: To make a solemn promise or statement under oath; it names the act of binding oneself to the truth.
entries.definitionCN: 在誓言下作出郑重承诺或陈述，强调的是让自己受真话约束的动作。

entries.definition: To give sworn evidence in a deposition, recorded before the trial rather than in open court.
entries.definitionCN: 在庭外录取的宣誓证词中作证，通常在审前进行。

entries.definition: To state formally that something is true, often as an alternative to swearing an oath.
entries.definitionCN: 正式声明某事为真，常用作宣誓的替代形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Testis 'witness' plus -fy 'make': to make someone a speaking witness.
normal.cn: testis「证人」加 -fy「使」：使人成为开口的证人。

normal.en: The family runs testify, testimony, testifier, testimonial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 testify、testimony、testifier 与 testimonial。

normal.en: Prepositions decide sides: testify against, testify for, testify to.
normal.cn: 介词决定立场：作证指控、为某人作证、证明某事。

normal.en: Objects testify too: the ruins testify to an older city.
normal.cn: 物品也会作证：废墟证明这里曾有更古老的城市。

normal.en: Contest and protest share the calling-of-witnesses root but add different prefixes.
normal.cn: contest 与 protest 共享「传唤证人」的词根，只是前缀不同。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised before the first word, not after it.
abstract.cn: 想象手在第一句话之前就已举起，而不是说完之后。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that keeps repeating what it saw, whether or not anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙不断重复它看见的事，无论有没有人问。

abstract.en: Picture two prepositions standing on either side of one witness.
abstract.cn: 想象两个介词站在同一位证人的两侧。

examples.en: Three former employees testified that the safety checks were skipped.
examples.cn: 三名前雇员作证说安全检查被跳过了。

examples.en: The empty shelves testify to how fast the town grew.
examples.cn: 空空的货架说明这座镇子发展得有多快。

examples.en: She was asked to testify to the date on the receipt.
examples.cn: 有人请她就收据上的日期作证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「test（作证）+ ify（使）」——使事实被说出来：作证、证实

root: 拉丁 testificari「作证」= testis（证人）+ facere（做、使）；testis 更深来源不确定。英语 testify 经古法语 testifier 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one witness through the building: into the stand, into a clause, onto one side of a case, then onto the other, out into objects, into a congregation, into a committee room and finally onto a point that the evidence is meant to settle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一位证人走遍整栋楼：走上证人席、进入从句、站到案件一方、再到另一方，随后走入物品、走进会众、走进委员会会议室，最后落在证据所要确立的那一点上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on the book, a voice giving an account in the order the events happened.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在书上，一个声音按事件发生的顺序把经过说出来。

branches.en: THE VOICE ON THE STAND: first the witness appears, then the content of the account is stated.
branches.cn: 证人席上的声音：先出现证人，再陈述叙述的内容。

branches.en: ONE SIDE: the same account is aimed at an accused person and counted against them.
branches.cn: 站在一方：同一段叙述被对准被指控者，成为对其不利的证据。

branches.en: THE OTHER SIDE: the account can equally be aimed in support, and only the preposition changes.
branches.cn: 站在另一方：同一段叙述也可以支持对方，变的只是介词。

branches.en: OBJECTS SPEAK: things make facts evident without any person taking the stand.
branches.cn: 物品开口：事物不需要任何人出庭，也能让事实变得清楚。

branches.en: OTHER ROOMS AND OTHER POINTS: a congregation, a committee and a fact to be established each borrow the courtroom verb.
branches.cn: 别的场合与别的落点：会众、委员会与待确立的事实都借用了这个法庭动词。

intro.en: Testify is a Latin verb whose root and second element still build English words.
intro.cn: testify 是一个拉丁动词，词根与第二个成分在英语中仍在构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin testis gives testimony, testament and testimonial; facere 'to make' gives -fy in testify and appears in many verbs of making.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 testis 衍生 testimony、testament 与 testimonial；facere「做、使」在 testify 中化为 -fy，并出现在许多表示「使……成为」的动词里。

items.example: The root names the person who speaks.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指开口说话的人。

items.example: The second element turns the witness into an action.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分把「证人」变成一个动作。

items.meaning: to make; to cause to be
items.example: The suffix builds verbs such as testify and verify.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 testify、verify 一类动词。

items.example: The mechanic testified before the judge.
items.exampleCN: 修理工作证于法官面前。

items.example: The testimony was recorded verbatim.
items.exampleCN: 证词被逐字记录。

items.example: The testifier spoke for twenty minutes.
items.exampleCN: 作证者讲了二十分钟。

items.example: Two clerks attested the deed.
items.exampleCN: 两名职员为这份契据作证。

items.meaningCN: 把证人一起传唤，故指争辩、竞赛
items.example: The two sides contested the result.
items.exampleCN: 双方对结果提出争议。
